Jay Meena Targets India's First Soft Tennis Medal

Indian soft tennis player Jay Meena has expressed confidence in securing India’s first-ever medal in the sport at the Asian Games. His assurance comes after he advanced to the men’s singles semi-finals at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 edition.

Meena’s progression to the semi-finals marks a significant milestone for Indian soft tennis on the international stage. The sport, while gaining traction, has yet to yield a medal for India in this premier multi-sport event.

By reaching the final four, Meena has positioned himself to compete for a place on the podium. His performance in the upcoming semi-final match will determine whether he advances to the final and potentially claims history for the country.

The Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games provide a crucial platform for Meena to showcase his skills against top competitors from across Asia. His journey to the semi-finals demonstrates his growing competitiveness in the global soft tennis circuit.

As the tournament progresses, attention turns to the semi-final clash where Meena will face a determined opponent. A win would secure his spot in the final and keep the dream of a historic medal alive.

What to watch: Jay Meena’s performance in the men’s singles semi-final match at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games.

ICC Chief Hails India’s Dominant Asian Games Cricket Victory

ICC chairman Jay Shah and BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia have extended their congratulations to the Indian women’s cricket team following their successful defense of the Asian Games gold medal. The team secured a commanding victory over Sri Lanka in the final match held in Nisshin on Tuesday, winning by a margin of 147 runs. This performance demonstrated the depth and skill of the Indian squad as they asserted their dominance in the tournament. Shah and Saikia’s presence at the venue underscored the high level of institutional support for the women’s team’s achievements. The 147-run margin highlighted the gap between the two sides, reflecting India’s strong batting and bowling displays throughout the match. This victory not only adds to India’s trophy cabinet but also reinforces their position as the leading force in Asian women’s cricket. The congratulatory remarks from cricket’s top administrators serve as a recognition of the team’s hard work and strategic execution. The win in Nisshin marks a significant milestone for Indian women’s cricket, continuing a streak of excellence in international competitions. The response from the cricketing community has been positive, with many praising the team’s composure and skill under pressure. This achievement is seen as a testament to the growing investment in women’s cricket in India.
